doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Order of Wallington, Mingus and Blakey; friendship with Art
summary: McLean sorts out the sequence of his jobs and says Art Blakey has advised him since he was seventeen.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You mentioned Blakey, and that’s – actually, the next major artist you’re working with is Charles Mingus. Is that correct?
I think I recall him being the next. You mean after George Wallington?
Did Wallington – Wallington was after Miles.

Wallington was after Miles, yeah. And then, after Wallington, I think I went – I’m pretty sure I must have gone with Mingus, but I’m not too sure that I didn’t play a little with Art. I’m not sure. But I think I may . . .
That period between Art and Mingus kind of went a little back and forth, in and out of both bands? Or how did that work?

That – it was circumstances. I was working with – Art and I were close, first of all, since I was about 17. I used to go to his house on 117th Street over there when he lived in Harlem, over there by Madison Avenue – Lenox Avenue – Fifth Avenue. So I knew him for many years. He’s always been someone that has advised me and kind of had an influence on me. Anyway, when I was with Mingus, and then Mingus and I had
that altercation in Cleveland, when he hit me, and I got – and fired me and left me stranded in the town, me and . . .
